standard.title: To and Fro (Jig Back) Movement Bi-Cable Ropeways — Code of Practice (Second Revision) (टू एंड फ्रो (जिग बैक) संचलन द्वि-केबल रज्जूमार्ग — रीति संहिता (दूसरा पुनरीक्षण))
standard.description: This Indian Standard covers the design, engineering, construction, safety installations, clearances, and operational maintenance of to and fro (jig back) movement bi-cable aerial ropeways used for the separate transportation of passengers and goods in cabins.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard covers the design, engineering, construction, safety installations, clearances, and operational maintenance of to and fro (jig back) movement bi-cable aerial ropeways used for the separate transportation of passengers and goods in cabins.

certification.description: Voluntary National Code. However, state government ropeway safety acts, municipal municipal-corporation clearances, and forest/environmental department permits across India make strict compliance with IS 5230 mandatory for ropeway licensing, safety certification, and commercial operation.
requirements: Final observed or calculated test and analytical values (such as clearances, specific speeds, friction limits, or dimensions) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 (or IS 2:2022). The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The crossing of routes, roads, railways, waterways, or other ropeways shall be avoided as far as possible to prevent mechanical collisions or clearance hazards.
Where crossings are unavoidable, vertical and horizontal clearances must be determined in such a manner that there is no danger for any vehicle using the various ways.

Crossings and paralleling with railways, highways, cableways, or overhead electric lines must be designed so that no mutual discomfort or hazard results during normal operation, rescue operations, or installation works.
Wherever local conditions are favorable and the characteristics of the electric lines permit it, overhead electric lines crossing the ropeway corridor shall be replaced by underground cables.
The minimum breaking strength of tensioning or regulating ropes shall be at least 5.5 times the maximum axial load in the rope during operation.
Telephonic and signal wire ropes must be of the stranded type and protected against corrosion (such as hot-dip galvanizing or polymer sheathing) to ensure clear communication.
Rope-socketing (splicing or socket-pouring) must be performed with utmost care. Only specialized organizations with proven experience in making rope sockets shall be entrusted with this operation.

A rope must be immediately withdrawn from service when the loss of strength in the rope due to wear, corrosion, broken wires, or a combination thereof is approaching one-sixth (16.67%) of the original strength.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves without lining (cast iron or steel) must equal 0.07.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves with leather lining must equal 0.15.
The coefficient of friction (µ) for drive sheave grooves with rubber or similar lining must equal 0.25 to prevent slippage.
Drive sheave grooves with aluminum lining may also be used, for which the value of µ must be agreed upon between the ropeway promoter and the Inspecting Authority.
The contact angle of the traction/haulage rope on the driving sheave must ensure that in the most unfavorable combination of circumstances, the required drive power is safely transmitted to the rope.
An automatic mechanical and electrical braking interlock must be triggered instantly if the normal stop or emergency stop push button is pressed by the operator.
